problem: Autonomous exploration of large outdoor environments usually depends on occupancy or frontier maps built from LiDAR, depth, GPS and IMU. Such maps are hard to build with only a monocular camera. RGB-only diffusion navigation policies such as NoMaD are goal-conditioned and explore only through policy variance, with no global novelty signal, so they revisit places and loop.
motivation: There is little expert data for exploration, and exploration admits many valid trajectories. The paper therefore asks how to make a pre-trained, imitation-learned navigation diffusion policy behave exploratively without exploration-specific training data. The driving observation is that in visually varied outdoor environments, visual novelty of imagined future views tracks geometric coverage. A world model can therefore score candidate actions by curiosity without any map or odometry.
key_idea: At inference time, optimize the initial noise distribution of a pre-trained waypoint diffusion policy with CEM. The objective is a visual-curiosity cost: a navigation world model predicts the future view for each candidate action, and patch-level reciprocal matching scores its novelty against a database of past observations.
insight: Two design choices matter. First, noise-distribution guidance works better than simply picking the best candidate. In the guidance ablation (figure only), greedy selection of the top-VCM candidate oscillates between competing directions at intersections and gets trapped in loops. In the time plots it sometimes falls below a random-selection baseline (NoMaD*), whereas updating the CEM noise distribution keeps useful stochasticity and commitment to a path. Second, the diffusion policy is an essential action prior (Table II, Town 1): replacing it with Gaussian action sampling plus CEM drops Area 12299→7072, APL 3.120→1.845, raises PF 0.03%→4.35%, and takes ~4× longer. Viewpoint-robust MASt3R reciprocal patch matching beats direct per-patch L2 (Area 11248, APL 2.856). Architecture also matters for safety: NoMaD's pooling before the context transformer and its EfficientNet encoder cause roughly 10× more collisions (0.278% vs 0.042% PF) than the VAE-based NoMaD* variant.
method: State encoding: the current frame I_t and T prior frames are encoded into patch-level latent states by a frozen VAE (Stable Video Diffusion / NWM VAE), then positionally encoded.

Diffusion policy: a context transformer (6 blocks, 8 heads, 256-d) pools tokens into a 1D conditioning vector c_t. A UNet DDPM denoiser (K=10 steps) outputs H relative (x,y) waypoints. Trained by imitation on CARLA BasicAgent trajectories; N noise samples give N candidate action sequences.

World-model imagination: a fine-tuned 'small' Navigation World Model (NWM) autoregressively predicts future latent states ŝ_{t+1..t+H} from context and each candidate's actions (Δx, Δy, yaw = arctan(Δy/Δx)).

Curiosity cost: the final predicted state ŝ_{t+H} is matched against a temporally subsampled database of visited states using MASt3R fast reciprocal nearest-neighbor patch matching. Per-state distance D is the mean Euclidean distance of the top-250 most distant matched patch pairs. Cost L_c is the minimum over the database, i.e. distance to the most similar past view (higher = more novel).

CEM noise guidance: draw N noises from N(0, I_{2H}), score the resulting candidates, and refit the noise mean from the top-r candidates for L iterations. The final noise is sampled from the updated distribution and fed to the policy. The distribution is reset to a standard Gaussian every P execution steps, and guidance is applied only when candidate actions show sufficient variance.
Execution: waypoints are tracked by a low-level PID controller, with replanning every 20 simulation steps (~1 s).

setting.backbone: Custom diffusion policy (frozen SVD/NWM VAE encoder + 6-layer context transformer + UNet DDPM, trained on CARLA and fine-tuned per town) + Navigation World Model 'small' (fine-tuned) + MASt3R fast reciprocal matching (algorithm on VAE patch features)
setting.training_data: Collision-free CARLA trajectories generated by CARLA BasicAgent between random waypoints in Towns 1-5 (scale not stated). Diffusion policy: base training 100 epochs (batch 256), then 20 epochs of fine-tuning per town. NWM-small: fine-tuned from original checkpoints on the pooled five-town data for 55 epochs. No exploration-specific data; guidance is training-free at inference.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (current frame + T prior frames)
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (relative (x,y) displacements over horizon H), tracked by a PID controller, replanning every 20 sim steps (~1 s)
setting.privileged: none (evaluated in the same towns used for training/fine-tuning; lamp posts removed from scenes)

numbers.eval_set_note: CARLA Towns 1-5, 3 random seeds per town, fixed number of simulation steps; towns are the same ones used for training/per-town fine-tuning (no official split)
numbers.backbone: Custom VAE+transformer+UNet diffusion policy + NWM-small world model
numbers.extra: Policy fine-tuned per town (20 epochs), NWM fine-tuned on all five towns; lamp posts removed; coverage measured on a 16 m^2 grid; Area in m^2, APL = area / path length (m), AvgPF = % of policy calls with collision averaged across towns
numbers.evidence: Table I: 'Mean performance metrics across five environments (Towns 1-5). Area: Total Area (m^2), APL: Area per Path Length (m), Avg PF: Average Policy Failure across towns.'

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (CARLA outdoor exploration), not comparable to standard embodied navigation benchmarks. The guidance-vs-greedy ablation and the APL-over-time curves appear only in figures, with no numbers. Table II (Town 1 ablations) reports Ours as Area 12299, APL 3.120, PF 0.03%. Its PF differs from Table I's town-averaged 0.046%. Its variants are w/o diffusion policy (7072 / 1.845 / 4.35%) and w/o fast reciprocal matching (11248 / 2.856 / 0.02%). Table I's Town 4 APL column header is printed as 'A/PL'.
results: VANDERER achieves the highest explored area and APL in all five CARLA towns. Examples: Town 2 area is 5488 m^2 vs 4368 for NoMaD (APL 2.79 vs 2.23), and Town 3 area is 14267 vs 12848 for NoMaD*. Overall it explores 13.4% more area on average than NoMaD. Its policy-failure rate (0.046%) is about 6× lower than NoMaD's (0.278%) and close to the best, NoMaD* (0.042%). It also beats an RND-based selection baseline (DP-RND) and greedy VCM selection.
limitations: Evaluated only in CARLA simulation, on the same five towns used for training and per-town fine-tuning. There is no real-robot or unseen-environment test, and lamp posts were removed to simplify scenes.

Relies on the hypothesis that visual novelty correlates with geometric coverage, which the authors limit to environments with sufficient visual variance. It may break in visually repetitive or indoor settings.

Heavy inference: N candidates × world-model rollouts × reciprocal matching against a database × L CEM iterations, with no runtime reported for the full method. There is also no comparison to map-based (frontier / RL-with-LiDAR) exploration methods.
compares_to: NoMaD* (NoMaD with VAE encoder and post-transformer pooling)
DP-RND (diffusion policy + Random Network Distillation selection)
